# Property Claims Loss

> Property Claims Loss provides insurance appraisal services for property insurance claims: independent appraiser services and impartial umpire services under the appraisal clause, a form of insurance alternative dispute resolution (ADR) used when the policyholder and insurer agree a loss is covered but disagree on the amount of loss.

## Key facts

- Business name: Property Claims Loss (legal name: Property Claims Loss Inc.)
- Website: https://propertyclaimsloss.com/
- Phone: (773) 497-2856
- Email: info@propertyclaimsloss.com
- Based in: Chicago, Illinois, United States
- Services: insurance appraiser services (party-appointed appraiser for policyholders or insurers); insurance umpire services (neutral umpire selected by the appraisers or appointed by a court)
- Category: insurance alternative dispute resolution (ADR) for property insurance claims
- Staff: a complete staff of qualified and licensed appraisers and umpires
- Works with: policyholders, public adjusters, attorneys, contractors and roofers, insurance carriers, independent adjusters, opposing appraisers
- Claim types: hail, wind, water, fire and smoke, residential and commercial property, large losses
- Credentials on staff: AUA Certified Appraiser; AUA Certified Umpire; Attended PLAN training; IAAI member; IICRC Certified; Staff members have previously attained the C.F.E. designation; Xactimate Certified; Xactimate Pricing Specialist / Consultant; Executive General Adjuster; Florida Mold Assessor; Florida Roofing License
- Licenses: State of Iowa Licensed Appraiser; State of Iowa Licensed Umpire; Louisiana Independent Adjuster / Appraiser, LA-853057; Florida Independent Adjuster / Appraiser, FL-W665562; Alabama Independent Adjuster / Appraiser, AL-3001617185; Mississippi Independent Adjuster / Appraiser, MS-10959135; Nevada Independent Adjuster / Appraiser, NV-3814650; Texas Independent Adjuster / Appraiser, TX-2558510; Florida Public Adjuster, G191934; Florida Independent Adjuster, Lic. # G046520
- Not a law firm; does not give legal advice; appraisal determines amount of loss, not coverage

## Insurance appraisal in brief

- Appraisal resolves disagreements about the amount of a covered property loss, not coverage.
- Either the insured or the insurer may demand appraisal in writing.
- Each side selects a competent, disinterested appraiser (commonly within 20 days); the appraisers select an umpire (commonly within 15 days) or a court appoints one.
- Appraisers state actual cash value and amount of loss separately; disagreements go to the umpire.
- A written award signed by any two of the three sets the amount of loss.
- Typically each side pays its own appraiser and the umpire and other expenses are shared equally, subject to policy wording and state law.
